item.title: Why Reading Correctly Matters: Stress, Dagesh and Meaning | Dikduk
item.description:
Why Hebrew is stressed on the last syllable, how a wrong stress or a missing dagesh changes a verse or a prayer, why pronouncing aleph and ayin is a halachic matter, and the Gemara's lessons on precise reading.

item.title: Shema, Not Shma: The Rules of Sheva and Kamats | Dikduk
item.description:
How the Hebrew letters should sound, the five rules of the sounded sheva, and the five cases where a kamats is read "o", with examples from the Shema and the Amidah.

item.title: How One Accent Changes the Meaning of the Shema | Dikduk
item.description:
Where does the stress fall, and why does it matter in the Shema? Taamim as stress and pauses, milra and milel, the dagesh kal in begad kefat and the dagesh hazak, with practical rules for accurate reading from a Humash with taamim.

item.title: The Maqam: How Middle Eastern Music Shapes Our Prayers | Dikduk
item.description:
The maqam, the Middle Eastern musical mode, shapes the melodies of Sephardi prayer. With the community Hazzan as guest, the class traces music in the Torah, the Talmudic hazzan, and how each maqam suits particular occasions, from Hijaz for sadness to Siga for the Shema.
